# Check — M0-c-01, the S3 slice: closing check of the session's hardening round S2 (lane check/M0-c-01-close-s2, flow flow-7, stage group S, 2026-10-19)

**Verdict: FAIL — one blocker.** All five failing lines of the round hold on this checker's own evidence:

* The R-28 slice share is FIXED, and R-31 and KI-10's seed are classed and REPORTED.
* N-c1c-1, N-c1c-2 and N-c1c-3 are PINNED.
* N-c1c-6 is FIXED (a comment).

The refusal census does not rise. NO-SHIFT holds. Every gate exits 0. The blocker is a new finding in the round's own
code. Targeted mutant **M8** removes `solvedAs.delete(later)` from F-WALL's re-draw in `siting/slice.ts`. It survives
the item's whole test folder. This checker's reach probe drives that branch on a lawful synthetic river site, and there
M8 changes the slice. So M8 survives on a promise the round states in so many words: C-0397 (1) "A re-draw replaces
the route T reads", and the header of `slice.ts`. The brief's rule makes such a survivor a blocker. The tree's own
behaviour is right; the defect is the missing pin.

## The new blocker: M8 survives on C-0397 (1)

**The mutant.** M8 deletes the line `      solvedAs.delete(later);` from F-WALL's coincidence branch of `s3Slice`
(`packages/layout/src/siting/slice.ts:145`). That line drops the deck rule's stored "route as (5) solved it" when
F-WALL re-draws the route's pick. Without it, T and the boundary keep reading the old pick's (5) route after the
re-draw. That route is no gate's route: it breaks C-0201 (6), which says T's road set is the gates' own routes, and
C-0397 (1), "A re-draw replaces the route T reads". M8 passes all 109 tests of `packages/layout/test/siting`
(`logs/mutants/M8.log`, `Tests 109 passed (109)`; CONFIRMED).

**Reach (CONFIRMED, `logs/reach*.txt`, `logs/m8.txt`).** The reach probe ran 5 700 slices on the small site
(`smallSite`, 400 ha frame, 30 ha walled). Each had a synthetic river band and one deck, and the probe varied the
band's width and position, the deck's y, N and the seed. The deck rule fired 244 times. The M8 branch (a re-draw of a
route the deck rule had re-solved) was reached once:

* `smallSite(3)`, a river band at x 200 – 220 m, a deck at y 100 m, `requestedN: 6`.
* On the tree: digest `656beddfac1f783d`. One deck re-solve of ordinal 5, then one F-WALL re-draw of it
  (`{"rung":"redraw","ordinal":5,"with":0,"attempt":1,"from":3562,"to":3722}`). T equals the field over the routes
  that stand (`T=(5)field:true`). 6 gates.
* Under M8: digest `6aa2ed47259c6e0c`. A second re-draw follows
  (`{"rung":"redraw","ordinal":5,…,"attempt":2,"from":3722,"to":2913}`), because T still reads the stale route.
  `T=(5)field:false`.

The input is lawful and of the same kind as the folder's own river layouts: `picks.test.ts` seed 25 uses the same
synthetic band and deck. `requestedN` is the slice's requested N₁. So M8 is reachable and not equivalent. The
families' NO-SHIFT cases never reach the branch (m8 = 0 in all 590), so no registered output is wrong today. That is
why the tree's behaviour is right and the defect is the missing pin. **BLOCKER (the brief: "a survivor on a stated
promise you do not find equivalent stays a BLOCKER"; CONFIRMED).**

**Required change (inside the item's owns).** Add a pin to `test/siting/` (`decks.test.ts` or `picks.test.ts`): a site
where F-WALL re-draws a route the deck rule has re-solved. This checker's witness above is one such site; the round
may build its own. The pin asserts:

* the redraw rung;
* that T equals `fieldT` over the routes that stand, with the re-drawn route as (5) solves it;
* that no second re-draw follows.

It must be red under M8. Then re-land the record.
